How to Submit Public Comment

Members of the Public who wish to submit public comment may do so using one of the
following methods. Public comment is limited to the time allotted, and comment for agenda
items 3 and 4 is combined.

In-Person: Complete a Speaker Card indicating the agenda item number and submit it to the
City Clerk prior to the meeting. Speakers shall be limited to three minutes per person (six
minutes if using an interpreter) per item. At the Mayor’s discretion, the time limit may be
shortened to allow all speakers to address the City Council. Please note that interactions
between the City Council, City staff, and the public during meetings are subject to the City’s
Rules of Decorum.

Website: Electronic submission of Public Comment is available via the online public comment
form at Public Comment. Public Comment submitted electronically by 4:00 P.M. on the meeting
day will be forwarded to the City Council before the meeting for their consideration, but will
not be read during the meeting. Comments submitted after 4:00 P.M. will be forwarded to
Council but may not be received before the meeting.

Via Zoom or Telephone: “Raise your hand” - Members of the public may speak by using the
“Raise Hand” function during the public comments portion, if on Zoom or telephone. Staff will
unmute speakers participating via Zoom or telephone and announce your name when it is your
time to speak. When calling in using a telephone press *9 to raise your hand and press *6 to
unmute yourself when called. Public Comments via Zoom or Telephone shall follow the
same rules as In-Person.

  6. CONTINUED BUSINESS – None.

 7. NEW BUSINESS

  A. DUMPLING AND BEER FESTIVAL 2026 FUNDING REQUEST FOR EVENT
  OPERATOR

  The Dumpling and Beer Festival (Festival) was introduced in 2015 to showcase
  the culinary aspect of the City and attract tourism to the Mission District. Over
  the years, the festival has grown into a community event that celebrates
  diversity and culture through popular food and drink. Each year the event
  attracts around 5,000 to 7,000 visitors and this number continues to grow. This
  report provides a summary of the Event Operators request for financial
  assistance to better support the production and execution of the 11th Dumpling
  and Beer Fest.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  With the recommendation of the Dumpling and Beer Fest Subcommittee, staff
  presents the following options for the City Council consideration:

  1. Make no changes to the current agreement (in-kind support only); or

  2. Review and approve $30,000 in financial support, amend the Professional
  Service Agreement with MPD Events accordingly, and authorize the City
  Manager to execute the Amended Agreement; or

  3. Review and approve $50,000 in financial support, amend the Professional
  Service Agreement with MPD Events accordingly, and authorize the City
  Manager to execute the Amended Agreement.

MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 1, 2026
  REGULAR MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL CITY COUNCIL

I  CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Chan called the regular meeting of the San Gabriel City Council to order at 6:33
  P.M. on Tuesday, September 1, 2026, in the Council Chamber at City Hall, 425 South
  Mission Drive, San Gabriel, California, 91776.

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Council Member Wu.

  ROLL CALL

  Council Members Present:  Jorge Herrera Avila, Denise Menchaca, John Wu, Vice
  Mayor Tony Ding, and Mayor Eric L. Chan.
  Council Members Absent:  None.
  Staff Members Present:  City Manager Mark Lazzaretto, Assistant City Attorney
  Martin Koczanowicz, Community Services Director

I  Rebecca Perez, Chief City Clerk Sharon Clark, Fire Chief
  Steven Wallace, Human Resources/Risk Management
  Director Edward Macias, Police Chief Edward Elizalde,
  Community Development Director David Sanchez,
  Public Works Director Michael Sledd, Acting Finance
  Director Linda Tang, and Assistant City Clerk Adam
  Yang.

  ANNOUNCEMENTS

  Chief City Clerk Clark provided information for the public on how to view the meeting.

  1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

  Mayor Chan approved the agenda order.

  2. PRESENTATIONS

  A. CERTIFICATE OF RECOGNITION FOR BROADWAY HEALTHCARE CENTER

I  Mayor Chan made the presentation to Broadway Healthcare Center Administrator
  Rithy Thong.

  B. POLICE DEPARTMENT PROMOTION RECOGNITION

  Police Chief Elizalde made the presentation.

  3. PUBLIC COMMENT

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 1 of 4  September 1, 2026
   Mary Cammarano, resident, spoke in favor of item 4C.

  Remote participant Caleb Schimke expressed various concerns about the Flock
  automated camera system used by the San Gabriel Police Department and other
  agencies.

  4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  A motion was made by Council Member Wu, seconded by Council Member Menchaca,

I  to approve Consent Calendar Items 4A - 4C as presented.

  Motion carried by a vote of 5-0 as follows:

  AYES:  HERRERA AVILA, MENCHACA, WU, DING, CHAN
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The City Council approved the Minutes of the Regular City Council Meeting of August
  18, 2026.

  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  The City Council approved August 7 and 14, 2026, Material Demands for the
  payment of City expenditures.

I  C. GRAPEVINE ARBOR FEE WAIVER REQUEST BY THE SAN GABRIEL HISTORICAL
  ASSOCIATION

  The City Council approved the fee waiver of the Grapevine Arbor building rental
  fees in the amount of $480 for the San Gabriel Historical Association's event on
  September 10, 2026.

  5. PUBLIC HEARING - None.

  6. CONTINUED BUSINESS - None

  7. NEW BUSINESS

  A. DUMPLING AND BEER FESTIVAL 2026 FUNDING REQUEST FOR EVENT
  OPERATOR

  Economic Development Manager Karen Ko and Matt De Miglio, C.E.O. of MPD
  Events made the presentation.

I  Clarifying discussion included a report from the City Council subcommittee of
  Mayor Chan and Council Member Herrera Avila in favor of the City providing up to
  $50,000 in financial support for event expenses; sponsorship, name of event, first-
  year of operation, and length of event challenges; City staff time freed by having
  an outside event operator; unlikelihood of the City realizing a refund of monies
  invested in the event; condition changes since award of the agreement; the
  proposed funding would improve infrastructure, commercial participation and user
  experience; with the request-for-proposals process, the terms can be negotiated
  even after award of agreement; expenses to be covered by additional City
  investment; and City expenses for the event.

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 2 of4  September 1, 2026
   RECESS AND RECONVENE

  The meeting was recessed at 8:28 P.M. and reconvened at 8:39 P.M. will all Council
  Members present.

  There was no public comment.

  Discussion included making an investment in this event; the importance of sticking

I  to an agreement; benefits to the community MPD Events is bringing to the event,
  lack of staff capacity, and intangible assets MPD Events will provide.

  A motion was made by Council Member Herrera Avila, seconded by Mayor Chan,
  to approve $50,000 in financial support, amend the Professional Service Agreement
  with MPD Events accordingly, and authorize the City Manager to execute the
  Amended Agreement.

  Motion carried by a vote of 3-2 as follows:

  AYES:  HERRERA AVILA, MENCHACA, CHAN
  NOES:  WU, DING
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

  8. CITY MANAGER'S REPORT

  City Manager Lazzaretto expressed appreciation for Council 's patience with the
  technological glitches during the meeting.

I  9. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Council Member Herrera Avila reported on his attendance at the Dumpling and Beer
  Fest subcommittee meeting.

  Council Member Wu reported on his attendance at a San Gabriel Valley Cities meeting
  with Taiwanese investors at CalTech, a farewell to Jason Kim of Paris Baguette,
  Legislative Night hosted by the West San Gabriel Valley REALTORS@, and a Chess
  Tournament hosted by the San Gabriel Valley Chess Club and Rooklogic at the
  Grapevine Arbor in support of the San Gabriel Police Officers' Association's annual
  Breast Cancer Awareness Project.

  Council Member Menchaca reported on her attendance at the Oh Sip! grand opening
  and the West San Gabriel Valley REALTORS® event; and announced Silent Movies at
  the Mission Playhouse and the 25 th Anniversary of 911 remembrance and tribute
  ceremony at 6:30 a.m. at San Gabriel Fire Station 51.

  Vice Mayor Ding reported on his attendance at a California Contract Cities Association

I  August Board of Directors Meeting, San Gabriel Valley Economic Partnership Taipei
  Computer Association Matchmaking Workshop, YWCA San Gabriel Valley 2026
  Champions of Change Awards Gala, West San Gabriel Valley REALTORS® Legislative
  Day Meet & Greet, and the Los Angeles Grace Lions Club Installation Ceremony.

  Mayor Chan reported on his attendance at a Contract Cities board meeting, monthly
  combined three Chambers of Commerce (Alhambra, Rosemead, Temple City)
  networking mixer, YWCA annual fundraising gala, and West San Gabriel Valley
  REALTORS® Meet & Greet; and invited the community to the 911 Remembrance

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 3 of 4  September 1, 2026
   Ceremony at Fire Station 51, 1313 S. Del Mar Avenue, San Gabriel, on September 11,
  2026, at 6:30 A.M.

  10. CLOSED SESSION - None.

  11. ADJOURNMENT

  The meeting was adjourned at 9:11 P.M.

I
  Respectfully submitted:

  J

  Approved this 15th day of September, 2026:

  ERIC L. CHAN, Mayor

I
